messages:
Alex (support): heads up — ACME just escalated. They got ~200 alert emails for `route.latency.p95 > 500ms` over a 12m window even though the console charts show mostly empty data during that time. sending repro steps below

Alex (support): repro (quick):
1) open console -> metrics -> route.latency.p95 (scope: org=acme)
2) set time range 2025-11-12 09:00–09:12 UTC
3) alert history shows repeated fires every 1m starting 09:02, but chart has 0s except a couple isolated points

Alex (support): raw query we used in support UI:```sql
SELECT time_bucket(60s, ts) AS bucket, max(value) as p95
FROM metrics.rollups
WHERE name = 'route.latency.p95' AND org_id = 'acme' AND ts BETWEEN '2025-11-12T09:00:00Z' AND '2025-11-12T09:12:00Z'
GROUP BY bucket
ORDER BY bucket;```

AlertBot: alerts/route-latency-p95 fired 198 times for org=acme between 2025-11-12T09:02 and 2025-11-12T09:11 (threshold 500ms)

Maria (eng-sre): can you paste the exact alert eval config? sliding window, period, and eval cadence? also any recent deploys to metrics ingest/rollup?

Alex (support): alert rule snippet from Console:```yaml
expr: max_over_time(metric('route.latency.p95'){org='acme'}[1m]) > 500
for: 30s
eval_interval: 60s
```
no recent changes on the rule. support checked account-level rollup settings and noticed some tenants have an `offset` set on the rollup job (legacy importer).

Sameer (eng-platform): suspicious — the rollup writer for legacy pipeline was writing timestamp at bucket_midpoint (`bucket_start + 30s`) for 1m rollups to make downsampling easier. alert eval assumes bucket-aligned timestamps (bucket_start). That mismatch can cause the evaluator's lookback window to sometimes include the same rolled point twice across adjacent windows.

Sameer (eng-platform): example timeline:
- rollup for 09:01 bucket written with ts=09:01:30 and value=600
- eval at 09:02 (looking at last 1m) requests data [09:01:02,09:02:02) and picks up ts=09:01:30 -> sees 600 => alert fires
- eval at 09:03 requests [09:02:02,09:03:02) but because of the midpoint timestamps some queries also pull the 09:01:30 point (depending on alignment) and you get another fire even though no new events happened

Priya (analytics): I pulled the raw rows for that window and confirmed there are rollup points at `:30` offsets for this org. snippet:```
ts                 | name                   | value
2025-11-12T09:01:30Z | route.latency.p95      | 600
2025-11-12T09:04:30Z | route.latency.p95      | 0
2025-11-12T09:07:30Z | route.latency.p95      | 620
```

Maria (eng-sre): ok that explains duplicate-firing. Two mitigation paths:
1) hotfix evaluator to align lookback windows to rollup offset when present (fast)
2) long-term: change rollup writer to stamp `bucket_start` (best for consistency) and backfill where necessary

Sameer (eng-platform): I opened a quick patch to the eval path to respect `rollup_offset` metadata if the queried metric has it. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1209 (draft) — it adds an `align_to_rollup` flag for the eval query. Will run unit + canary.

Alex (support): pushed patch to customer so they stop getting pagers? can we backfill or suppress historical duplicate alerts so ACME doesn't get stale flurries?

Sameer (eng-platform): for immediate relief: set `suppress_duplicate_fires: true` on that alert rule for the org (console supports per-org overrides). I toggled that for ACME at 09:30 UTC — confirmed alert counts dropped.

Priya (analytics): after suppression + patch to evaluator in canary, I reran the alert evaluation offline on the same data and the spurious fires disappear. also queued a migration to rewrite legacy rollups to bucket_start timestamps during nightly maintenance (ticket INF-4521).

Alex (support): ACME support note: emailed them with explanation + ETA for full fix and offered to mute notifications until migration completes. They acknowledged. :thumbsup:

Maria (eng-sre): next actions
- Sameer: finish PR and deploy canary to staging; roll to prod after 2h of green (owner: Sameer)
- Platform: schedule rollup timestamp migration and backfill (owner: analytics, Priya)
- Support: monitor ACME and escalate if any other tenants show same pattern (owner: Alex)

Sameer (eng-platform): ongoing — will update thread with canary link and rollout time. planning a small DB write to normalize future rollups and a retained mapping for legacy offsets to avoid surprise.

Alex (support): thanks all. customer on call at 16:00 PT so will update after that.

Priya (analytics): noted incident for postmortem? low-sev but customer-visible. I'll create INF-PM-2025-11-12 and add analysis + graphs.

Maria (eng-sre): thx. tagging for visibility: @Sameer @Priya @Alex. closing here once PR is in prod. :white_check_mark:
